land.text: Văn Lang, 'ruled by the Lạc Việt', whose 'lands were described as tidelands'

predecessors.note: Văn Lang (the Hùng kings) has no Cliopatria row; semi-legendary, it matches the Đông Sơn culture ('c. 7th century BC to 1st century CE'). Listed under counterparts_needing_dossiers.

land.text: Nam Cương, 'ruled by the Âu Việt', who 'lived south of the Zuo River, in the You River basin, and in the upper Lô, Gâm, and Cầu river areas'

predecessors.note: Thục Phán's own realm; no Cliopatria row. Listed under counterparts_needing_dossiers.

land.text: all of Âu Lạc, 'annexed' in 179 BC and 'divided ... into the Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen Commanderies'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Nanyue shapes already include the Red River delta from 206 BC, so Nanyue's dossier should agree on 179 BC or the two overlap for 27 years.

capitals.name: Cổ Loa
capitals.note: Infobox capital; 'Cổ Loa, the largest prehistoric moated urban settlement in Southeast Asia'; An Dương Vương 'ordered the fortified settlement built'; construction 'might have begun as early as the fourth century BCE'. Coordinates are the researcher's (Đông Anh, Hanoi).

keyframe_review.note: Years only: from 257 BC ('Founded in 257 BCE by Thục Phán'; infobox 'Established: 257/208 BCE'), one year before Cliopatria's. 140,776 km2 covering the Red River delta and the hills to the Zuo and You rivers fits 'parts of modern-day Guangxi and northern Vietnam' and the Âu Việt lands 'south of the Zuo River, in the You River basin, and in the upper Lô, Gâm, and Cầu river areas'. No infobox area to compare.

Years only: to 179 BC. 'in 179 BC Zhao Tuo marched southward and successfully annexed Âu Lạc' (Nanyue page); the Âu Lạc lead: 'succumbed to the state of Nanyue in 179 BCE'. Cliopatria's 207 BC follows the traditional 208/207 date the infobox also gives. Cliopatria's Nanyue shapes include the delta from 206 BC, an overlap the Nanyue dossier must settle.

region.text: the Lạc lands of the Red River delta and the Âu Việt hills 'south of the Zuo River, in the You River basin, and in the upper Lô, Gâm, and Cầu river areas'

ledger.note: 257 BCE: Thục Phán conquers Văn Lang and founds Âu Lạc at Cổ Loa. 'In approximately 257 BCE, Văn Lang was purportedly annexed by the Âu Việt leader Thục Phán', who 'overthrew the last Hùng kings, unified the two kingdoms, and proclaimed himself An Dương Vương'; infobox: 'In 257 BCE, Nam Cương, ruled by the Âu Việt, conquered Văn Lang, ruled by the Lạc Việt, and formed Âu Lạc'. The page gives the peoples' lands, not a boundary; the shape is Cliopatria's. Other sources put the kingdom at 208–179 BCE (infobox 'Established: 257/208 BCE').

179 BCE: Zhao Tuo annexes Âu Lạc. 'in 179 BC Zhao Tuo marched southward and successfully annexed Âu Lạc'; Nanyue 'divided Xiang Commandery into the Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen Commanderies' (undated). The Âu Lạc page: the campaign came 'after Empress Lü's death (180 BCE)', with 'troops and bribes against the Minyue, Western Ou, and Luo', and 'Zhao Tuo then incorporated the regions into Nanyue but left the indigenous chiefs controlling the population'; its infobox gives 208/179 BCE, Cliopatria 207 BC.

wars.name: Nanyue conquest of Âu Lạc (179 BC)
wars.outcome: 'in 179 BC Zhao Tuo marched southward and successfully annexed Âu Lạc'; the land became the Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen commanderies of Nanyue.
wars.note: The Âu Lạc page says Taylor (1983) 'argued that Âu Lạc only temporarily acknowledged Nanyue', undated: a possible tributary interval between 204 and 179 BC that no page dates, so it is not in the ledger.

certainty.note: A protohistoric kingdom known from Chinese and later Vietnamese texts; the shape is Cliopatria's throughout and the hill frontier toward the Zuo and You rivers is approximate.

sources.title: Âu Lạc
sources.note: Identity, infobox (257/208 to 208/179 BCE, Cổ Loa, Nam Cương and Văn Lang, Nanyue), the Âu Việt lands, Cổ Loa's dating, the 180 BCE campaign. No infobox area; the page has no Qin war.

sources.title: Nanyue
sources.note: Nanyue founded 204 BC at Panyu; 'in 179 BC Zhao Tuo marched southward and successfully annexed Âu Lạc'; the Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen commanderies; 111 BC.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Âu Lạc' 256–207 BC (2 identical shapes) kept; dated 257–179 BC from the pages. The end is the main decision: the infobox gives 208/179 BCE, the lead and the Nanyue page 179 BC, Cliopatria (and Vietnamese tradition) 207/208 BC. 179 BC is used; the alternative is noted in both keyframes. Consequence: Cliopatria's Nanyue shapes include the Red River delta from 206 BC, so Nanyue (slug nanyue, group ea-02 or the Lingnan group) and Âu Lạc overlap 206–179 BC unless the Nanyue dossier adopts 179 BC for the gain of Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen; flagged in problems.

Not on the pages opened: the Qin campaigns against the Yue (Cliopatria's Qin row 218–209 BC) and any Qin commandery in Âu Lạc's hills; a dated tributary interval under Nanyue (Taylor's 'temporarily acknowledged'); Cổ Loa's construction is dated by archaeology ('between 300 and 100 BCE'), not by the founding. Predecessors Văn Lang and Nam Cương have no Cliopatria rows and are semi-legendary (Đông Sơn culture); the slugs van-lang and nam-cuong are placeholders listed under counterparts_needing_dossiers, not new dossiers of this batch. Gazetteer: 'Red River Delta' resolves.
